messages.subject: RE: CANOPY
messages.body_plain:
Hi Aisha,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. To detect somatic point mutations from tumor sequencing files is important and non-trivial however that is not the focus and contribution by Canopy. There are many methods developed for calling point mutations, for example, GATK, Mutect, Mutect2, VarScan2, etc. For our case, we don’t have a matched normal or normal to detect somatic mutations and thus we adopted the GATK UnifiedGenotyper, followed by stringent QC procedures to make sure that the variants called are truly somatic. The bash script for GATK we put on Canopy’s website is just for reference and is not maintained by us (but rather the GATK group in Broad). With this said, I will try to answer your questions.

1.       We use joint calling.

2.       We didn’t adopt VQSR but use Annovar to annotate all the variants and adopt stringent QC procedures (e.g., they aren’t called in the 1000 Genomes Project, they don’t reside in segmental duplication regions, and they are categorized as deleterious by scoring metrics such as CADD etc.).

Hope that this is of help to you.

Yuchao

From: Aisha Yousaf [mailto:aisha...@live.com]
Sent: Monday, August 7, 2017 4:59 AM
To: Jiang, Yuchao <yuc...@wharton.upenn.edu>
Subject: CANOPY

Hi Jiang,

I hope you are doing well.  I am interested to perform the analysis on MDA-MB-231 as you did in your article using CANOPY. Previously, I asked you for exome targets. Thank you for providing the targets. Until now, I have called variants using Unified Genotyper (based on the code you provided on GitHub). However, I have few questions regarding  MDA-MB-231 variant calling and filtration. Due to them, I am unable to move ahead.

As per MDA-MB-231 example in CANOPY paper,

 Should I call variants on all samples together and get a single VCF output or individually on each samples and then merge them?
How did you filter the variants in that particular case? According to GATK , we cannot apply VQSR (Variant Quality Score Recalibration) to less than 30 exomes.

Thanks for your time and any possible help in this regard.

Best wishes,

AISHA

messages.subject: Re: Canopy
messages.body_plain:
Hi Georgette,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. Canopy is designed to deconvolute bulk tumor samples that are collected at different time points or at different locations (i.e., multiregion sequencing). I don’t think a single sample per patient would tell us much about the heterogenous structure and thus Canopy will not be the method to consider for this case.

You can try Pyclone, SciClone for point mutations, and Sequenza, TITAN for CNVs.

Hope this is of help.
Yuchao
